properties.article_text_excerpt: Procurorii polonezi au anunțat luni că inițiază o anchetă pentru o posibilă „infracțiune cu caracter terorist”, după incendiul de noaptea trecută de la o fabrică de drone din Skarzysko-Kamienna, potrivit AFP. Fabrica este a WB Electronics, un grup privat specializat în sisteme electronice de apărare. Potrivit un comunicat al parchetului, ancheta a fost deschisă pentru „participare la activități ale unui serviciu de informații străin împotriva Republicii Polonia și pentru o infracțiune cu caracter terorist, constând în provocarea deliberată (…) a unui incendiu pe terenul uzinei WB Electronics, cu ajutorul unei încărcături care conținea materiale inflamabile”, notează Agerpres . Procurorii nu au menționat numele țării pe care o suspectează că a comandat incendiul la fabrica de la Skarzysko-Kamienna, la 140 km sud de Varșovia. properties.article_text_excerpt: At least 547 people have been killed in flash floods triggered by a glacier collapse in Nepal, police said on Friday. Chinese authorities previously confirmed that at least five more people had been killed in neighbouring Tibet, which is controlled by Beijing. This brings the overall death toll from Wednesday’s disaster in the Nepal-Tibet border region to 552. In addition, Indian authorities have recovered seven bodies from a river flowing from Nepal. The victims are also believed to have died in the devastating floods. More than 1,400 people, including hundreds of foreign tourists, are still reported missing. Several dozen Latvian nationals are also among those reported missing. Nepalese police said that 3,253 people have been evacuated by helicopter from the disaster zone, many of them injured. properties.article_text_excerpt: Russia currently poses no direct military threat to Latvia, although a number of signs point to potential longer-term plans, Latvia’s Constitution Protection Bureau (SAB) said. According to SAB’s assessment, Vladimir Putin’s regime continues to operate under a distorted perception of threats, reinforced by the Kremlin elite’s growing isolation and the absence of critical internal views. Russia’s attitude towards Western countries, including Latvia, is becoming increasingly hostile and aggressive. SAB, in cooperation with other EU and NATO intelligence and security services, continues to monitor the situation and developments in the region. SAB’s observations indicate that Russia’s perception of Latvia is becoming increasingly similar to the way it viewed Ukraine before launching the war. This could lead to more aggressive Russian activities over the longer term, significantly increasing security risks for Europe.
